### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 17ed9e7bfd65532d83109273837e4a44624dee5c`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 17ed9e7bfd65532d83109273837e4a44624dee5c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2e463bc314cda36cdd51b7aa039eb87a54052583` — the merge of head `e010381489b0cd259652b6a121070254423536d0` into base `17ed9e7bfd65532d83109273837e4a44624dee5c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2e463bc314cda36cdd51b7aa039eb87a54052583 && git checkout 2e463bc314cda36cdd51b7aa039eb87a54052583
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 17ed9e7bfd65532d83109273837e4a44624dee5c e010381489b0cd259652b6a121070254423536d0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 17ed9e7bfd65532d83109273837e4a44624dee5c && git merge --no-ff e010381489b0cd259652b6a121070254423536d0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 17ed9e7bfd65532d83109273837e4a44624dee5c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 17ed9e7bfd65532d83109273837e4a44624dee5c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

1. **Changeset misses `@objectstack/platform-objects`.** The diff regenerates 11 `metadata-forms` translation bundles and their source hashes in `packages/platform-objects` (the new `Fields` row of the field-group sub-form). That package is published (`files: ["dist", …]`) and the bundles ship with it, but `.changeset/35900-field-group-members.md` lists only spec, lint and app-shell (l1-face `changeset` FLAG). `added` takes at least `minor` on every package the diff moves, so add `'@objectstack/platform-objects': minor`. #35921 lists the same package for its two bundles.

Overlaps to expect on merge: `object.zod.ts` `ObjectFieldGroupSchema` (#35921 rewrites the `relatedList` describe next to the new `fields` key) and `ObjectGroupInspector.tsx` (#35921 switches its picker to `isPlaceable`; this PR adds the member count and clears `fields` when a related list is chosen). Whichever lands second merges main and re-runs those files' tests.
3. No browser run. The record page and both forms read the new order only through `deriveFieldGroupLayout`, which is pinned directly, so this is not blocking. One run of the card's first acceptance line (`fields: ['account', 'name']` puts 客户 first on the record page and in the form, desktop and 375) would still be worth having before landing.

### Checked and fine

- **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, `Fixes #35900` with no other closing keyword. Merging delivers every item on the card, so `Fixes` is right. `Skills-docs: follow-up #35902` is true: #35902 covers 「分组列字段」.
- **Card item 4, the four conflicts.** Each has a parse or derivation test: a listed field whose own `group` names another group is refused at `fieldGroups[i].fields[j]` and at `fields.<name>.group`; a field two lists name is refused at the second listing; a `group` naming a listing group that leaves the field out is appended after the list; an unlisted field with no `group` goes to the untitled bucket. A repeat inside one list is refused too (claim reading 2). Item 5: `fields` on a `relatedList` group is refused.
- **No new key, same behaviour.** A group without `fields` resolves as before: own `group`, declaration order. Every new refusal needs the new key, so nothing that parsed on `main` is refused. That is right for `added`, and the batch20 pin that refused `fieldGroups[].fields` as guidance now accepts it, on purpose.
- **One derivation for every reader (item 6).** `git grep deriveFieldGroupLayout` at this head finds the record page (`record-details.tsx`, `buildDefaultPageSchema.ts`, `recordDetailSections.ts`), the forms (`plugin-form/fieldGroups.ts`, console `FormPage.tsx`), Studio, and the lint rules (`object-field-groups.ts`, `validate-field-consumers.ts`, `i18n-walk.ts`). Each picks the list up without its own edit. The remaining direct `field.group` readers are unrelated: the book resolver groups docs, and `plugin-security` reads its own platform object's group.
- **Studio (item 7).** The new pin checks that a reorder inside a group writes only `fieldGroups` and leaves `fields` the same object. A cross-group move lists the field and drops its contradicting `group`. Only the untitled bucket, which has no list, still reorders declarations. A field no list names stays visible through its `group` or the bucket, which covers the card's AI-build line.
- **Lint.** `field-group-member-unknown` warns on a listed name that is neither declared nor injected, and an injected `owner_id` is spared.
- **Prose read sentence by sentence:** the changeset and the `Field.group` TSDoc and describe. Both match the diff. The generated `content/docs/references/**` is covered by `check:generated`.
- **Overlap.** `buildDefaultPageSchema.ts` and the form plugins are untouched, as the claim said, so #35891's and #35889's regions are clear.
- **Gates.** At `53409dca`: 12 success, 9 expected skip, 0 failed, 26 pending, and the floor checks are not reported yet. Vitest was NOT MEASURED by L1. After finding 1, I read only the delta and give ACCEPT on a green head.

Every completed check-run on the head concluded success or skipped; none failed. One `Check Changeset` run (started 20:22Z, after a PR-body edit) was still in progress when read; the earlier `Check Changeset` run on the same head concluded success.

### ① Derived judgments

- `ObjectFieldGroupSchema.fields` (optional array of snake_case field names) is a new authorable key. Right as a widening: on `main` the strict group shape refused `fields` with a guidance message, so no document that parses today changes meaning. The `object-strictness-batch20` pin moved with it.
- The four new refusals in `refuseFieldGroupMembershipConflicts` (a list on a `relatedList` group, a repeat in one list, a field two groups list, a listed field whose own `group` differs) fire only when a group carries a `fields` array. Right: none narrows today's accept set.
- `deriveFieldGroupLayout` for input with no list on any group: walked against the `main` loop, the result is the same (declared-group membership through `Field.group`, hidden filtered, an explicitly grouped system field kept, ungrouped system fields left out, empty groups dropped). Right.
- New public exports `readFieldGroupMembership` and `FieldGroupMembership` from `@objectstack/spec/data`; api-surface and export-origins regenerated. Right.
- `Field.group`: description only, accept set unchanged. Right.
- `@objectstack/lint`: new warning `field-group-member-unknown`; rules (b) and (d) read membership through `readFieldGroupMembership`. Right: a warning, and the two older rules only stop misreporting list members.
- `object.form.ts`: a `tags` row for the new key; generated translation bundles follow. Right.
- The object document SERVED to a caller under field-level security: wrong, see M1. The served-document mask does not know the new key, so the list this PR publishes does not reach such a caller.

### ② Semver level

The changeset bumps `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@objectstack/platform-objects` and `@object-ui/plugin-detail` at minor. That matches what the diff publishes: one new optional key, one new export, one new lint warning, new Studio behaviour, regenerated form translations, and a changed manifest description. Nothing in the diff removes or narrows a published shape, so no major is owed.

Clause-②: yes (widening) — the same line is on the PR body and in the changeset, and it agrees with the diff. `Metadata-protocol: added` is on both and agrees with the claim amendment 7046460603.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Dev report `out_of_scope_findings`: no dedicated canvas test for `ObjectFormCanvas` add / move-to-group. Answered: accepted for this face. Both paths write through `writeGroupLayout` or append to an existing list, and the remainder is the lane seat's ACCEPT.
- Claim reading (1), a listed name the object lacks is skipped and lint warns: holds in the tree (`resolveFieldGroupMembership` skips it, the parse does not judge it, lint rule (e) warns, an injected column does not warn).
- Claim reading (2), refusals as new-key shape rules: holds, with the wider-than-stated case in S1.
- Claim reading (3), the ungrouped bucket still reorders field declarations: holds in `writeGroupLayout` (only the bucket's own declaration slots are permuted). The card's acceptance line speaks of a drag inside a group, which this does not touch; the changeset states the exception.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up #35902`: the card's AI-builder acceptance line holds structurally (a field no list names shows through its own `group` or the ungrouped bucket); teaching the new spelling is deferred to #35902.
- SQL push-down: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. Nothing to find.
- Overlap with #35921 and #35923 in `object.zod.ts`: out of scope; nothing in them shows this contract inconsistent.

### ④ Design judgment

M1 (must-fix) — `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`, the `fields` contract ("decides which fields the group shows and in what order, on every surface that renders the group"), does not hold for a caller with any listed field denied by field-level security. `packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.ts` (not in the diff) scrubs the served object document; its `fieldGroups` block classifies `key, label, icon, description, collapse, defaultExpanded, collapsible, collapsed, visibleWhen, relatedList` and nothing else. `scrubRecord` sends an unlisted key to `unclassified`, which removes the whole key when its value mentions a denied name. So when one name in `fieldGroups[i].fields` is denied, the entire list is deleted from the document `applyObjectSchemaMask` serves (REST `meta-item-read-gate.ts` and `rest-server.ts`, and the MCP bridge). The client then derives with the older rule. Under the spelling this PR recommends, and the one Studio writes (it drops a moved field's own `group`), the readable members carry no `group`, so the section disappears and its fields fall into the untitled bucket in declaration order; for a group Studio converted from the older spelling, the order reverts and moved fields leave the group. Nothing leaks (the fail-safe over-masks), but the record page and both forms silently lose the layout for exactly the users FLS exists for. The fix is to classify the key as a name list (`fields: names`, which filters the denied entry and keeps the rest), pin it with a test beside the existing `fieldGroups` cases, and correct that module's note that readable fields join a group "through their own `group`". The module's closed-set pin covers top-level `ObjectSchema` keys only, which is why the head's checks are green; extending it to the nested group shape is a follow-up, not part of this fix.

S1 (should-fix) — `object.zod.ts` `refuseFieldGroupMembershipConflicts` refuses a listed field whose own `group` is ANY string other than the listing group's key (`own === key` is the only pass). Every contract sentence in the diff (`ObjectFieldGroupSchema` design rules, the `fields` jsdoc and describe, `Field.group`, the form help text, the docs page, the changeset) and the card's rule say "names another group". A `group` naming an undeclared key is not another group: on `main` it means ungrouped, and lint reports it as `field-group-undeclared`. The gap is reachable through Studio's own output: a first drag inside an older-spelling group writes the list while the members keep `group: KEY`; renaming that group's key in the metadata form then makes every listed member's `group` name an undeclared key, and the save is refused at two paths per member. `object.form.ts` still tells the author on the `key` row that renaming it "leaves them ungrouped", which is no longer true for listed members in either reading. No test pins the undeclared case. Decide one way: judge only a `group` that names another DECLARED group (the list already wins in the layout, and lint already warns about the stale key), or keep the wider refusal and say "any other value" in each sentence; either way add the test and correct the `key` help text.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):
- `object.zod.ts`, the guidance block of `ObjectFieldGroupSchema`: the comment "Membership is declared the OTHER WAY ROUND ..." introduced the `fields` guidance entry this PR deletes. It now sits above `order` and says the opposite of the new contract.
- `object.zod.ts` tombstone guidance for `detail` and `defaultDetailForm`, and `packages/lint/src/object-field-groups.ts` hints (named in the claim's file surface, not in the diff), still teach only `Field.group` on member fields. Follow-up with #35902.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts` `identityAdminGroupFields` reads `SysUser` fields by `field.group === 'Admin'` to build the withheld field set. It is a non-layout reader of the older spelling: moving `sys_user` to group lists would silently empty that set. Not touched here; worth a line on the follow-up card before any platform object is migrated.

Held, after trying to break it:
- `field-group-layout.ts`: listed names resolve first-listing-wins with an own-property test against `fields`, so `constructor` or `__proto__` in a list places nothing; hidden fields are filtered after membership, so `readFieldGroupMembership` and the layout agree on who belongs where; a list on a `relatedList` group is not read, matching the parse refusal. The module header's rule list matches the code sentence by sentence.
- `field.zod.ts`: the `group` jsdoc and describe match the derivation (same group allowed, left-out field appended after the list).
- `object.form.ts`: the `fields` row matches the schema; only the `key` help text is off (S1).
- `validate-semantic-roles.ts`: membership comes from the spec helper over declared plus injected columns, so lint and the layout cannot disagree; rule (e) skips `relatedList` groups, which the parse already refuses.
- `liveness/object.json`: the `fields` row names real readers (`readGroup`, `resolveFieldGroupMembership`) and both consumers pass `fieldGroups` through unchanged (`plugin-form/src/fieldGroups.ts`, `buildDefaultPageSchema.ts`).
- `object-fields-io.ts` `writeGroupLayout`: a changed group gets a list, an unchanged group is returned as the same object, a moved field's contradicting `group` is dropped, fields the canvas does not show are kept at the end of the list, and `fields` is written only for the ungrouped bucket's own slots. Its output never trips the four refusals. `ObjectFormDesigner`, `ObjectFormCanvas`, `ObjectFieldInspector` and `ObjectGroupInspector` read and write through it; choosing a related list clears the list.
- `plugin-detail`: description and comment text only, and they match the derivation.
